title: Planning-node lookup lives in the template module
description:
Move the pure lookup that finds a container's bracket planning node, and the container-label interpolation it depends on, out of `commands` into `crate::templates`, so the validation layer stops importing it from `commands`.

## Background

- `find_planning_node` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:2280-2305`), `PLAN_DOC_LABEL` (`:2319`) and `planning_node_plan_path` (`:2328-2334`) are pure functions over issues and a `GraphTemplate`. `commands/mod.rs:96` re-exports the two functions for `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:682-683`, an inverted dependency from the validation layer onto `commands`.
- `find_planning_node` calls `declared_container_label` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template_expand.rs:626-653`, `pub(super)`), which interpolates container tokens through `InterpolationContext` (`template_expand.rs:528-610`). Template application also uses both (`commands/template.rs:14-15,916`; the `template_expand.rs` tests at `:1221-1303`).
- `crate::templates` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs`) already owns `GraphTemplate` (`:279`), `RoleBindings` (`:226`) and `GraphTemplate::plan_doc_location` (`:511`), and imports nothing from `commands`.
- Callers: `commands/validate.rs:967-968` (`plan_document_paths`), `:1042-1043` (`plan_content_with_issues`), `validation/repository.rs:682-683` (`project_plan_content`), `commands/template.rs:916`, and the unit test `test_find_planning_node_resolves_template_declared_container_label` (`commands/validate.rs:2537`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `find_planning_node`, `planning_node_plan_path`, the plan-document label and `declared_container_label`, with the container-token interpolation they use, are defined under `crate::templates`; `commands` defines and re-exports none of them.
- [hard] REQ-02: `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs` resolves planning nodes through `crate::templates`, and no production code under `crates/jit/src/validation/` names a `crate::commands` item for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Template application and validation resolve the same planning node and container label as before: the moved unit test passes in the templates module, and the template-application and scope-validation suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Planning-node and container-label resolution move from commands into crate::templates.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure lookup moves between modules with its import sites and one test.

title: One resolver for plan-document references
description:
Resolve a breakable container's plan document in one function, make every site that needs it call that function, and merge the two plan-content readers into one.

## Background

The chain breakable type → container template with a plan-document location → planning node (`crate::templates::find_planning_node`, `crates/jit/src/templates.rs:658`) → planning node's `plan`-labelled document reference (`planning_node_plan_path`, `:685`) is written three times:

- `plan_document_paths` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:998-1019`) derives the paths a validation capture must read;
- `plan_content_with_issues` (`commands/validate.rs:1056-1102`) reads the content for graph-rule evaluation and serves the mutation callers (`commands/mod.rs:2773,3191`, `commands/dependency.rs:382`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:377`);
- `project_plan_content` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:633-668`) reads the content inside repository validation.

`plan_content_from_image` (`commands/validate.rs:1033-1052`) is a second content reader: it parses the image's issues leniently and forwards to `plan_content_with_issues`. Its callers already hold the issues (`commands/issue.rs:129`, `commands/validate.rs:1155`, `commands/gate_check.rs:458,534`) except `image_plan_content` (`validate.rs:1614-1623`).

The content readers share one rule: an absent plan whose planning node is not `done` is omitted, and an absent plan whose planning node is `done` is an error. The scope-validation tests over external plans (`crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/scope_validation_tests.rs:984-1215,1327,1356`) exercise the rule end to end.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One pure function in `crate::templates` maps a container, the issues by id and the template registry to the container's plan-document reference, or none, together with whether its planning node is `done`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `plan_document_paths`, the plan-content reader and `project_plan_content` obtain plan-document references only through that function; no other code walks from a breakable type to a planning node's plan document.
- [hard] REQ-03: One function reads plan content from an image for given issues; `plan_content_from_image` no longer exists, each of its callers passes the issues it holds, and `image_plan_content` passes the issues its capture holds.
- [hard] REQ-04: One templates unit test owns the resolution cases: an inline plan (no reference), a relinked non-default path, and the not-done and done planning node; the scope-validation suite passes unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Plan-document references resolve through one function, and plan content is read through one function.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three copies of one resolution and two copies of one reader collapse in one focused change.

title: Configuration accessors for content format and strictness
description:
Make `JitConfig::content_format()` and `JitConfig::strictness()` the only readers of the repository's default content format and validation strictness: delete the two wrappers that still sit in front of them and give the accessors their own tests.

## Background

- `JitConfig::content_format()` (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:1209-1214`) and `JitConfig::strictness()` (`:1220-1225`) apply the defaults when `[validation]` is absent, delegating to `ValidationConfig::content_format()` and `ValidationConfig::strictness()` (`:258-266`), which apply them when the key is absent. Loading rejects an invalid token. The validation layer and most command sites already call them (for example `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:542`, `commands/mod.rs:1219-1220`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:609`, `commands/template.rs:1100`).
- Two wrappers remain. `repo_content_format` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/projection_render.rs:244-246`, called at `:102`) only forwards to the accessor. `CommandExecutor::repo_content_format` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2726-2729`) wraps it in a `Result` over the cached configuration and is called from `commands/validate.rs:1581,1680,1844,2001`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:608` and `commands/item.rs:152,307,389`.
- No unit test covers either accessor; `config.rs:1921,1932,1949,2097` cover token parsing only.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `JitConfig::content_format()` returns the repository's content format, Markdown when undeclared, and `JitConfig::strictness()` returns its strictness, loose when undeclared; each default is stated once, in the `ValidationConfig` accessor the `JitConfig` accessor delegates to.
- [hard] REQ-02: Neither `repo_content_format` function exists; each former caller reads the content format through `JitConfig::content_format()`, and no code outside `config.rs` maps an absent `[validation]` value to a default.
- [hard] REQ-03: Config unit tests show both accessors' result for an absent `[validation]` table, an absent key and a declared value, and the existing suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The content-format and strictness defaults are read only through the JitConfig accessors, which have their own tests.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two forwarding wrappers go, their eight call sites read the accessor, and the accessors gain tests.

title: Built-in validation pass names are one validation-layer vocabulary
description:
Declare the rule names of the built-in validation passes as one closed vocabulary in the validation layer, so `crates/jit/src/validation/` no longer imports them from `commands`.

## Background

- `DANGLING_LINK_RULE`, `ENFORCEMENT_DRIFT_RULE` and `REVIEW_PLACEHOLDER_RULE` are `&str` constants in `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:12,19,23`, re-exported at `commands/mod.rs:97`. Repository validation reads them from `commands` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:622,646,769,832`), and spells the fourth built-in name, `rules-file`, as a literal (`:215`). `commands/validate.rs:1605` spells it again.
- Other readers: `commands/validate.rs` (dangling, drift and placeholder passes), `commands/gate_check.rs:513,592,597` and tests (`validation/repository.rs:1006,1236,1263`, `commands/gate_check.rs:2908,3048`, `crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/item_cli_tests.rs`, `cli_item_validate/validate_cli_rule_tests.rs`, `cli_repo_workflow/profile_acceptance_tests.rs`).
- Closed vocabularies are declared through the crate's wire-vocabulary macro (`domain/vocabulary.rs`), which emits `as_str`, `ALL`, `FromStr` and serde from one list.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `BuiltInPass` vocabulary in the validation layer, declared through the wire-vocabulary macro, names `rules-file`, `dangling-item-link`, `enforcement-drift` and `review-placeholder`, and every built-in finding takes its rule name from it.
- [hard] REQ-02: The three `commands` constants and their re-export no longer exist, and no code spells a built-in pass name as a string literal outside the vocabulary declaration and tests that assert wire output.
- [hard] REQ-03: Findings keep their wire rule names: the existing validation and gate suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The built-in pass rule names become a closed vocabulary in the validation layer.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One closed vocabulary replaces three constants and one literal at a known set of sites.

title: Local rules compile each schema once per report
description:
Share one `SchemaEngine` across the issues repository validation evaluates, so each local rule's JSON Schema compiles once per report instead of once per issue.

## Background

- `evaluate_local` (`crates/jit/src/validation/local.rs:230`) desugars each matching rule's schema (`rule_schema`, `:272-278,343`) and builds a new `SchemaEngine` per call (`:289-290`). The engine already caches compiled validators by schema key (`crates/jit/src/validation/engine.rs:113-119`, `validator_for` `:317`, test `test_validator_is_cached_not_recompiled` `:947`), but the cache lives only for that one call.
- Repository validation calls `evaluate_local` once per issue (`collect_rule_findings`, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:543-552`), so each schema compiles once per issue.
- Single-issue write paths also call `evaluate_local` (`commands/mod.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/bulk_update.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`), as do its tests (`validation/local.rs`, `repository_state/default_rules.rs`, `tests/fast_docs_templates/content_format_dispatch.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/example_rulesets_tests.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs`). `SchemaEngine` is `!Sync`, which suits a single-threaded report.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Local-rule evaluation accepts a caller's `SchemaEngine`, and repository validation evaluates every issue against one engine per report, so each distinct schema compiles once per report; no new compiled-rule-set type is introduced.
- [hard] REQ-02: `evaluate_local` keeps its signature and evaluates against an engine of its own, so its callers are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test evaluates two issues against one shared engine and shows that a schema both match is compiled once.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Repository validation evaluates its issues against one shared schema engine, so each schema compiles once per report.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One engine parameter in local.rs plus its one repository-validation consumer.

warning_overrides.chain-link: Changes local.rs's engine ownership and one loop in collect_rule_findings; pure-validation-report, its neighbour on repository.rs, rewrites the report entry points around it, and folding a criterion-owning schema change into that build-reason change would grow the largest core entry.

title: Graph findings record their firing subject
description:
Record on every graph finding the issue whose rule application fired it, so a selection can tell the firing subject apart from the issue the finding is attributed to.

## Background

- `GraphFinding` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:262-307`) carries `issue_id` (attribution) and a private config-error flag. Constructors: `for_issue` (`:277`), `unattributed` (`:289`), `issue_finding` (`:742`) and `config_error` (`:753`); `evaluate_one` (`:600-690`) dispatches the assertion kinds.
- Attribution and subject differ in two cases: a `label-coverage` finding with `container-from-label` is attributed to the resolved container while the breakdown issue fired it (`:960-1060`), and a pointer that resolves to no issue or to several is a configuration error with no attribution although one issue fired it (`resolve_container` call sites in the same range).
- `label-uniqueness` findings (`:692-731`) and rule-level configuration errors have no firing subject.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GraphFinding` exposes `subject: Option<IssueId>`: the firing issue for every finding produced while applying a rule to one issue, configuration errors raised for one firing issue included, and `None` for `label-uniqueness` findings and rule-level configuration errors.
- [hard] REQ-02: Graph unit tests show a `container-from-label` coverage finding attributed to the container with the breakdown issue as subject, an unresolvable pointer reported as a configuration error whose subject is the firing issue, and a `label-uniqueness` finding with no subject.
- [hard] REQ-03: Attribution, messages and severities are unchanged, and the existing graph and validation suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Each graph finding records the issue whose rule application produced it, separately from its attribution.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One field set by the existing finding constructors inside graph.rs.

title: Issue-id prefixes match without allocating
description:
Make `IssueIdPrefix::matches` compare a prefix against a candidate issue id without allocating, removing the per-candidate allocation that dominates container-pointer and coverage-label resolution.

## Background

- `IssueIdPrefix::matches` (`crates/jit/src/domain/identity.rs:345-347`) normalises the candidate on every call: `normalise` (`:402-407`) allocates a lowercase, hyphen-free copy of the id before the `starts_with` test. The prefix already holds its own normalised form.
- Graph evaluation calls it once per candidate issue. `resolve_container` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:1090-1101`) tests every issue for each `container-from-label` pointer, from `evaluate_label_coverage` (`:743`) and `graph_rule_plan_source_ids` (`:431`), so resolution is O(pointers × issues) allocations; `label_credits_id` (`:122-143`) calls it for every crediting label (`:129,140`). Storage prefix resolution calls it per listed id (`crates/jit/src/storage/mod.rs:110`).
- A release-build profile of `jit validate` on this repository attributes about 29% of inclusive time to that normalisation (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/investigation.md`, capture part, C4).
- Matching is covered by the identity property tests (`identity.rs:863-916`) and the container-pointer graph tests (`graph.rs:2320,2473,2515,2548,2583`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `IssueIdPrefix::matches` decides whether the prefix names a candidate id without allocating; `resolve_container`, `label_credits_id` and storage prefix resolution keep calling it, and `GraphEvaluationContext` is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every caller resolves exactly as before: unique, ambiguous and unresolved container pointers, crediting labels and storage prefixes, the minimum prefix length included; the existing identity, graph and storage tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A property test shows that `matches` agrees with comparing the normalised candidate, for generated ids and for prefixes in any case and hyphenation.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: IssueIdPrefix::matches compares a prefix with a candidate id without allocating a normalised copy of the id.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One comparison inside one domain method changes, with one property test.

title: Item links resolve against one address index with item kinds resolved once
description:
Make item-link validation resolve every qualified link against one address index value, and resolve the configured item kinds once per set of captured declarations.

## Background

- `collect_item_link_findings` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:697-843`) builds a set of canonical addresses from issue-embedded items and project sources (`:713-749`), then resolves each issue-scoped address by scanning every issue with a prefix (`:800-814`).
- Item kinds are resolved by `resolve_item_kinds` in that pass (`:703`) and again for every rendered projection inside the same validation (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/projection_render.rs:67`, reached from `repository_state/materialize.rs:319`).
- Captured declarations are parsed once into `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:435-490`).
- Item kinds hold their id pattern as an `IdPattern`, kind scope is the domain `KindScope`, and item-address issue segments are `IssueIdPrefix` values.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A domain address-index type holds the canonical addresses of every issue-embedded and project item and resolves an issue-scoped address's prefix in one lookup; repository validation builds it once per validation and resolves every link label against it.
- [hard] REQ-02: `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` resolves the configured item kinds once, and item-link validation and projection rendering read them from there; neither calls `resolve_item_kinds`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests over the address index show a resolved project address, a resolved issue-scoped address given by short prefix, an alias-form address resolving like its canonical form, an ambiguous issue scope and a dangling address; the existing item-link tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged. An invalid item-kind declaration still fails the effective-configuration pass with the same error.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Repository validation resolves item links through one address index, and resolves item kinds once from the captured declarations.

title: One loader parses the issue records
description:
Parse every listed issue record through one loader, and make repository validation, validation capture and mutation bases call it.

## Background

Since c47d78c8, issue membership comes from the captured `.jit/issues` listing (`captured_issue_ids`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/index.rs:118-126`) and `.jit/index.json` holds tombstones only. Three loaders parse the listed records:

- `load_records` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:378-401`) checks that the index parses (`:380-384`), then parses every listed record with `serde_json` and checks its embedded id, reporting each defect as `RepositoryJudgedInvalid`.
- `effective_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:785-799`) decodes the overlay-effective bytes of every listed record through `decode_issue_record` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/issue_record.rs:18`) during capture.
- `captured_active_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2161-2185`) decodes the same records through `decode_issue_record`, reports a missing record as issue-not-found and a mismatched embedded id as an error; mutation bases, gate checking, archive and gate commands call it.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the three private loaders are replaced together, and an uncalled private function fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One function in `repository_state` parses every listed issue record from a byte source into parsed records, in listing order, checking embedded ids; its errors are typed.
- [hard] REQ-02: `effective_issues` and the record parsing in `load_records` and `captured_active_issues` no longer exist; each former caller calls the loader.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each caller keeps its contract: mutation captures still return the listed issues in listing order and report a missing record as issue-not-found, and repository validation reports a missing, unparseable or mismatched record, and an unparseable index, with today's messages.
- [hard] REQ-04: Unit tests own the loader's cases: a well-formed set, a missing record, a mismatched embedded id, and an unparseable record.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Listed issue records are parsed by one loader shared by validation, capture and mutation bases.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three private loaders converge on one new loader; deleting them makes the change one unit.

title: One pure function computes the validation report
description:
Replace the two repository-validation entry points and their `Result` pair with one pure function that computes a `ValidationReport` from a captured validation and the inputs its caller supplies.

## Background

- `validate_repository` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:169-202`) derives the materialization plan and calls `validate_repository_with_materializations` (`:204-357`) with both verdict arguments `Ok(())`; both return `Result<RepositoryValidationReport, RepositoryValidationFailure>` (`:52-132`), where the failure carries the partial report.
- `validate_repository_with_materializations` takes two verdicts computed outside the image as `Result<()>` arguments (`:208-209`): record fidelity, which becomes the structural failure (`:261-265`), and document-reference resolution, which `validate_integrity` raises (`:403-430`). Only `capture_validation_report` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:522-583`) computes them: `capture_document_reference_validation` (`:940-964`) captures each reference in its own bounded image, and `capture_record_fidelity_validation` (`:969-994`) captures every gate run and reads the whole event log through `RepositoryMutationSession::read_history_log`, outside `CaptureSpec`. Its two callers are whole `jit validate` and the `repository_validation` gate checker (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:1083-1086`), the history readers f8a6b298 names under its DEC-19.
- The function is not pure: `collect_rule_findings` reads the wall clock. The machine-local claims-index check that `validate_repository` also ran was deleted by f8a6b298's lease work (merge 96be25331), so validation reads nothing under `.git/jit/`.
- Callers: `commands/validate.rs` (`validate_silent` `:139`, `validate_repository_report` `:498`, `validate_repository_report_with_divergences` `:510`, `capture_validation_report` `:522`, `capture_repair_plan` `:655`), `commands/gate_check.rs` (`repository_rule_report` `:413`, `gate_findings_from_report` `:598`, the repository checker at `:1083-1086`), `commands/init.rs:164`, `commands/profile.rs:1084`, `commands/config.rs:293`, `main.rs` (the whole-repository branch of the `Commands::Validate` arm), the tests in `validation/repository.rs` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/undeclared_taxonomy_tests.rs:175`. Initialization, configuration and profile application judge proposed overlay images without history verdicts and read the report directly.
- The validation layer parses records through the shared records loader.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the report type replaces a `Result` pair whose callers only compile together.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `validation::report(&CapturedValidation, &ReportInputs) -> ValidationReport` is the only function that computes the repository report. `CapturedValidation` pairs a captured image with the records the loader parsed from it, and `CapturedValidation::from_image` parses them. `validate_repository`, `validate_repository_with_materializations`, `RepositoryValidationReport` and `RepositoryValidationFailure` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: The report reads only its arguments. `ReportInputs` carries the evaluation instant; while the claims-index check exists, the claims-index problems the executor computes from its own worktree paths with today's test-mode skip; and an optional history input holding the record-fidelity and document-reference verdicts. `crates/jit/src/validation/` reads no clock, environment, machine-local file or event-log history and calls no `crate::commands` function.
- [hard] REQ-03: `ValidationReport` exposes the passes reached, the structural failure if any, whether it carries history verdicts, and the findings projected to the wire `RuleReport`; a structural failure keeps every finding collected before it, and a failed history verdict is a structural failure as today.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every listed caller computes the report through the new function. Whole `jit validate` and the repository-validation gate are the only callers that supply the history input; `jit validate`, `config set`, `init`, profile apply and the repository-validation gate keep their output and exit status; the existing suites pass, and a unit test shows that an injected instant decides a `gate-recency` finding.

## Notes

- The history verdicts stay computed by the executor under its mutation session; this change moves only how they reach the report.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: A single pure validation-layer function computes the whole-repository report from a captured image and injected inputs.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The report type replaces a Result pair whose callers only compile together.

title: Validation capture hands its parsed records to the report
description:
Make the validation capture return the records it already parsed, so the report, the divergence view, document-reference discovery and record fidelity read them instead of parsing every issue again.

## Background

- `capture_proposed_base_inner` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:334-486`) parses every issue during capture to plan the closure (`:447-472`) and returns the image with those issues; `capture_proposed_base` (`:216-234`) drops the issues and returns the image alone.
- `capture_validation_report` (`:522-584`) then parses the issues again three times: `captured_divergences` (`:715-747`) through `captured_active_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2161`), document-reference discovery through `captured_active_issues` (`validate.rs:562`), and the report through its records pass (`load_records`, `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:378`).
- Record fidelity (`record_drift`, `crates/jit/src/validation/record_fidelity.rs:21-66`) decodes every issue record a fourth time: `issue_drift` (`:74-79`) parses the stored bytes to a JSON value, decodes an `Issue` from it, and compares the writer's serialization with the canonical form of the stored value. `index_drift` (`:68-71`) parses the index a second time after the records pass (`repository.rs:380-384`). Record fidelity runs only for the two history readers, whole `jit validate` and the `repository_validation` gate checker.
- Capture parses the overlay-effective bytes before the overlay is applied, which equals a parse of the overlaid image.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The validation capture returns a `CapturedValidation` holding the index and records it parsed, and the CLI validation path, `--fix` repair planning, document-reference discovery and the divergence view read those records; on this path the index and each issue record are decoded once.
- [hard] REQ-02: `captured_divergences` derives divergences from the captured records and parses nothing.
- [hard] REQ-03: Record fidelity takes the captured validation's parsed records and index plus the stored bytes it compares, and decodes no issue record or index again; it reports the same records as before.
- [hard] REQ-04: Output is unchanged: the validation, divergence, repair and record-fidelity suites pass unchanged.

## Decisions

- **D-01** — Steward ruling 2026-11-04: `--fix` repair planning decodes no issue record, since it consumes none. The hierarchy-fix, transition and reduction steps of `--fix` still decode through their own mutation sessions until the single-capture `--fix` replaces them. `jit recover` no longer depends on issue records; `jit validate` still reports a malformed record. Rejected: restoring a strict record check in recover; restructuring the other `--fix` steps here.
- **D-02** — Steward ruling 2026-11-04: record decoding keeps the typed decode's behaviour for repeated keys. A repeated issue field is rejected with its line and column; a repeated unknown or map key loads as before. The single value decode only notes a repeated key, and the typed decode then decides. Rejected: rejecting every repeated key, which is stricter than before (REQ-03, REQ-04).

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Whole-repository validation parses its records once, during capture, and the report reads them.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One capture return value changes for its three in-module consumers.

title: Shared test fixture for repository images
description:
Give tests one way to build a closed `RepositoryImage` from declared entries, listings and pinned evidence, without a storage backend or a mutation session.

title: Validation views are selections of the report
description:
Give `ValidationReport` the provenance each finding needs and a selection operation, so every validation view can be computed as a filter of the one report.

## Background

- `ValidationReport` holds findings projected to the wire `ReportedFinding` (`crates/jit/src/validation/report.rs:24`), which keeps the attributed issue, rule, severity and message only. A view also needs each finding's origin (local rule, graph rule and whether it is repository-wide at transition, or a built-in pass), its firing subject (graph findings record it) and whether it is a configuration error. The report also records whether it carries the history verdicts (record fidelity and document references), which only whole `jit validate` and the `repository_validation` gate checker supply; a failed verdict is part of the structural failure.
- Today each view filters its own pipeline: per-issue in `run_rules` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1643-1758`), scope in `validate_scope` (`:1833-1950`), explain in `explain_rules` (`:1993-2081`), single rule in `rule_validation_outcome` (`:1114-1174`), whose `RuleSelectionFault` (`:1177-1201`) the CLI renders as one error finding and the rule checker records as an `error` run, and the gate checkers in `crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:413-564`.
- Scope membership comes from `domain::queries::bracket_scope_ids` (`crates/jit/src/domain/queries.rs:372`) with the container template's breakdown type; rule selection errors come from `validation::graph::select_graph_rule` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:409`); explain rows use `Selector::match_failure` and `render_selector` (`commands/validate.rs:2040,2357-2376`, tests `:2851,2862`).
- The membership of each selection is fixed by the plan's `selection-membership` contract (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/plan.md`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each report finding carries its origin, firing subject, attribution and configuration-error flag, and the wire projection is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: `ValidationReport::select(&Selection)` returns the wire `RuleReport` for `Whole`, `Issue`, `Scope` and `Rule` selections through one membership predicate, and `ValidationReport::explain` returns the `ExplainReport` for an issue. A prefix that resolves to no issue or to several fails with today's not-found or ambiguity error; a report without parsed records fails every selection but `Whole` with its structural error; a `Whole` selection from a report without history verdicts fails with a typed error; a rule that cannot be selected for the issue returns its `RuleSelectionFault`.
- [hard] REQ-03: `render_selector` and the explain grouping live in the validation layer.
- [hard] REQ-04: Example unit tests show each selection's membership on one report, including the stated changes: a scope counts a coverage child outside the container's dependency closure, an issue selection omits a configuration error fired by another issue, an issue selection omits `enforcement-drift` and keeps `rules-file`, and only `Whole` reports a failed record-fidelity or document-reference verdict.

## Notes

- Behaviour changes, delivered to users as each view adopts the selection: scope rules see the whole repository; issue and explain configuration errors narrow to the selected issue's subject or rule; issue, explain, scope and rule selections report `rules-file` for an unloadable rule set; issue and explain selections never include `enforcement-drift`.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: ValidationReport answers whole, issue, scope, rule and explain selections through one membership predicate.

- `run_rules(None)` (`:1724-1754`) is a second whole-repository report. Its only production caller passes `Some` (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:6006`, inside `if id.is_some()`); its test callers are `commands/batch_create.rs:1069`, `commands/validate.rs:3284`, `commands/gate_check.rs:2979,3415`, `tests/fast_docs_templates/batch_export_tests.rs:455` and `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs:110`.
- The validation capture returns a `CapturedValidation` with the records it parsed. Whole-repository validation also derives the divergence view and the claims-index input and, as a history reader, the record-fidelity and document-reference verdicts; the issue selection excludes the structural failure.
- Other callers: `main.rs:5940` (explain), `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs` and `tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs:145`.
- Tests that re-prove filtering: `commands/validate.rs:3263`; `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs:97,117,152`; `tests/cli_item_validate/validate_cli_rule_tests.rs:611,631`.

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit validate <id>` and `--explain` call `ValidationReport::select(&Selection::Issue(..))` and `ValidationReport::explain` directly on the report computed from one validation capture whose parsed records the report reads; no per-view wrapper remains (`run_rules` and `explain_rules` are deleted), and neither path reads storage, the executor's caches, a second capture, the event-log history or the gate-run listing. title: One pure validation report over parsed records
description:

- [hard] REQ-05: Plan-document references, the content-format default and the strictness default each come from one function.

## Notes

`crates/jit/src/validation/record_fidelity.rs` adds a record-fidelity pass to whole-repository `jit validate`: stored index, issue, gate-run and event-log records must decode and reproduce what the writer would publish. It reads every gate run and the whole event log, so only whole `jit validate` and the built-in `repository_validation` gate checker run it, as the history readers f8a6b298 names under its DEC-19. It reaches the report with document-reference resolution as an optional history input, and the repository checker judges through the same function, history included, so a gate cannot pass where `jit validate` fails.
